reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses thermal stability of nanocrystalline HEA films via low grain-boundary energy and elemental segregation, but does not mention Cr-rich oxide networks, pre-oxidation treatments, or wear. E2 reports a discontinuous, partial Cr-O passive layer on a different Mo-HEA coating surface in aqueous corrosion, not a continuous grain-boundary oxide network formed by pre-oxidation for wear resistance. The premises are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Pre-oxidation at 600°C forms a continuous, nanocrystalline Cr-rich oxide network along grain boundaries in FeNiCrCoCu
This oxide network pins the microstructure and limits grain-boundary sliding and microcrack propagation
Limiting grain-boundary sliding and microcrack propagation enhances overall wear resistance at 500–700°C
FeNiCrCoCu thin films have a nanocrystalline microstructure with grain boundaries susceptible to sliding/cracking at high temperature
